full_name: Stochastic Gradient Sliding for Composite Convex Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Corollary 8.3)

problem.description: Composite convex programming with a smooth convex component f, a nonsmooth convex component h, and a relatively simple convex function chi.

variable_space.math: X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ is a closed convex set, }\chi\text{ is a relatively simple convex function, and } f:X\to\mathbb{R}\text{ and }h:X\to\mathbb{R}\text{, respectively, are general smooth and nonsmooth convex functions}.

assumptions.name: NonsmoothGrowth_8_1_3
assumptions.math: h(x) \le h(y)+\langle h'(y),x-y\rangle+M\|x-y\|,\quad \forall x,y\in X,\quad \text{for some }L>0\text{ and }M>0,\text{ where }h'(x)\in\partial h(x).

assumptions.name: SFO_Independence_Section8_1
assumptions.math: \xi_t \text{ is a random vector independent of the search points }u_t.

initialization.math: x_0\in X\text{ and iteration limit }N.\; \beta_k\in\mathbb{R}_{++},\;\gamma_k\in\mathbb{R}_+,\;T_k\in\mathbb{N},\;k=1,2,\ldots,\text{ are given and }\bar{x}_0=x_0.

steps.name: SPS inner initialization
steps.ref: Algorithm 8.1 PS procedure, PDF lines 28952-28954; inherited by Algorithm 8.2, PDF lines 29538-29544

steps.name: SPS stochastic prox update
steps.math: u_t=\operatorname{argmin}_{u\in X}\{g(u)+\langle H(u_{t-1},\xi_{t-1}),u\rangle+\beta V(x,u)+\beta p_t V(u_{t-1},u)+\chi(u)\}.

main_theorem.statement_math: Assume that \{p_t\} and \{\theta_t\} in the SPS procedure are set to (8.1.39). (a) If N is given a priori, \{\beta_k\} and \{\gamma_k\} are set to (8.1.40), and \{T_k\} is given by \[T_k=\left\lceil \frac{N(M^2+\sigma^2)k^2}{\tilde{D}L^2}\right\rceil,\] for some \tilde{D}>0. Then under Assumptions (8.1.6) and (8.1.7), we have \[\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le \frac{2L}{N(N+1)}[3V(x_0,x^*)+4\tilde{D}],\quad \forall N\ge 1.\] If in addition, X is compact and Assumption (8.1.57) holds, then \[\operatorname{Prob}\left\{\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)\ge \frac{2L}{N(N+1)}\left[3V(x_0,x^*)+4(1+\lambda)\tilde{D}+\frac{4\lambda\sqrt{\tilde{D}\bar{V}(x^*)}}{\sqrt{3}}\right]\right\}\le \exp\{-2\lambda^2/3\}+\exp\{-\lambda\},\quad \forall \lambda>0,\forall N\ge 1.\] (b) If X is compact, \{\beta_k\} and \{\gamma_k\} are set to (8.1.42), and \{T_k\} is given by \[T_k=\left\lceil \frac{(M^2+\sigma^2)(k+1)^3}{\tilde{D}L^2}\right\rceil,\] for some \tilde{D}>0. Then under Assumptions (8.1.6) and (8.1.7), we have \[\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le \frac{L}{(N+1)(N+2)}\left[\frac{27\bar{V}(x^*)}{2}+\frac{16\tilde{D}}{3}\right],\quad \forall N\ge 1.\] If in addition, Assumption (8.1.57) holds, then \[\operatorname{Prob}\left\{\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)\ge \frac{L}{N(N+2)}\left[\frac{27\bar{V}(x^*)}{2}+\frac{8(2+\lambda)\tilde{D}}{3}+\frac{12\lambda\sqrt{2\tilde{D}\bar{V}(x^*)}}{\sqrt{3}}\right]\right\}\le \exp\{-2\lambda^2/3\}+\exp\{-\lambda\},\quad \forall \lambda>0,\forall N\ge 1.\]
main_theorem.rate: Expected suboptimality O(L/N^2) for both parameter policies; high-probability deviations have the same O(L/N^2) scaling under the light-tail assumption.

key_lemmas.name: CompositeProxInequality_Lemma3_5
key_lemmas.statement_math: Let the convex function p:X\to\mathbb{R}, the points \tilde{x},\tilde{y}\in X, and the scalars \mu_1,\mu_2\ge 0 be given. Let \nu:X\to\mathbb{R} be a differentiable convex function and V(x,z) be defined in (3.2.2). If \[\hat{u}\in \operatorname{Argmin}\{p(u)+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},u)+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},u):u\in X\},\] then for any u\in X, we have \[p(\hat{u})+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},\hat{u})+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},\hat{u})\le p(u)+\mu_1V(\tilde{x},u)+\mu_2V(\tilde{y},u)-(\mu_1+\mu_2)V(\hat{u},u).\]
key_lemmas.role: Provides the three-point prox inequality used to analyze each SPS inner update.

proof.description: Use the first-order optimality condition for the prox subproblem.
Expand each Bregman term with the three-point identity following from the definition of V.

key_lemmas.name: WeightedRecursion_Lemma3_17
key_lemmas.statement_math: Let w_k\in(0,1], k=1,2,\ldots, be given. Also let us denote \[W_k:=\begin{cases}1,&k=1,\\ (1-w_k)W_{k-1},&k\ge 2.\end{cases}\] Suppose that W_k>0 for all k\ge 2 and that the sequence \{\delta_k\}_{k\ge 0} satisfies \[\delta_k\le (1-w_k)\delta_{k-1}+B_k,\quad k=1,2,\ldots.\] Then, we have \[\delta_k\le W_k(1-w_1)\delta_0+W_k\sum_{i=1}^k(B_i/W_i).\]
key_lemmas.role: Telescopes the weighted one-step recursions in both the SPS inner loop and the SGS outer loop.

proof.description: Divide the recurrence by W_k and use the definition of W_k.
Sum the divided inequalities from i=1 to k.

key_lemmas.name: SPSInnerBound_Proposition8_3
key_lemmas.statement_math: Assume that \{p_t\} and \{\theta_t\} in the SPS procedure satisfy (8.1.20). Then for any t\ge 1 and u\in X, \[\beta(1-P_t)^{-1}V(u_t,u)+[\Phi(\tilde{u}_t)-\Phi(u)]\le \beta P_t(1-P_t)^{-1}V(u_{t-1},u)+P_t(1-P_t)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^t(p_iP_{i-1})^{-1}\left[\frac{(M+\|\delta_i\|_*)^2}{2\beta p_i}+\langle \delta_i,u-u_{i-1}\rangle\right],\] where \Phi is defined in (8.1.19), \[\delta_t:=H(u_{t-1},\xi_{t-1})-h'(u_{t-1}),\quad\text{and}\quad h'(u_{t-1})=\mathbb{E}[H(u_{t-1},\xi_{t-1})].\]
key_lemmas.role: Bounds the stochastic inner prox-sliding error by a Bregman distance term plus accumulated oracle noise.

key_lemmas.name: MartingaleLargeDeviation_Lemma4_1
key_lemmas.statement_math: Let \xi[t]\equiv \{\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots,\xi_t\}\text{ be a sequence of iid random variables, and }\zeta_t=\zeta_t(\xi[t])\text{ be deterministic Borel functions of }\xi[t]\text{ such that }\mathbb{E}_{|\xi[t-1]}[\zeta_t]=0\text{ a.s. and }\mathbb{E}_{|\xi[t-1]}[\exp\{\zeta_t^2/\sigma_t^2\}]\le \exp\{1\}\text{ a.s., where }\sigma_t>0\text{ are deterministic. Then }\forall \lambda\ge 0:\; \operatorname{Prob}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^N\zeta_t>\lambda\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^N\sigma_t^2}\right\}\le \exp\{-\lambda^2/3\}.
key_lemmas.role: Supplies the large-deviation estimate used in Theorem 8.2 for the martingale-difference linear noise terms.

key_lemmas.name: CompactPolicyInnerSumBound_8_1_52
key_lemmas.statement_math: For the compact-policy parameters \(p_t=t/2\), \(\theta_t=2(t+1)/(t(t+3))\), \(\beta_k=9L(1-P_{T_k})/[2(k+1)]\), \(\gamma_k=3/(k+2)\), and \(\Gamma_k=6/[k(k+1)(k+2)]\), the SPS expected-noise inner summation satisfies \[\sum_{i=1}^{T_k}\frac{\gamma_kP_{T_k}}{\Gamma_k\beta_k(1-P_{T_k})p_i^2P_{i-1}}\le \frac{8k(k+1)^2}{9LT_k}.\]

key_lemmas.name: SGSGenericConvergence_Theorem8_2
key_lemmas.statement_math: Suppose that \{p_t\}, \{\theta_t\}, \{\beta_k\}, and \{\gamma_k\} in the SGS algorithm satisfy (8.1.20) and (8.1.25). (a) If relation (8.1.33) holds, then under Assumptions (8.1.6) and (8.1.7), we have, for any N\ge 1, \[\mathbb{E}[\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)]\le \tilde{B}_d(N):=\frac{\Gamma_N\beta_1}{1-P_{T_1}}V(x_0,u)+\Gamma_N\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^{T_k}\frac{(M^2+\sigma^2)\gamma_kP_{T_k}}{\beta_k\Gamma_k(1-P_{T_k})p_i^2P_{i-1}},\] where x^* is an arbitrary optimal solution of (8.1.1), and P_t and \Gamma_k are defined in (8.1.18) and (8.1.32), respectively. (b) If in addition, X is compact and Assumption (8.1.57) holds, then \[\operatorname{Prob}\{\Psi(\bar{x}_N)-\Psi(x^*)\ge \tilde{B}_d(N)+\lambda\tilde{B}_p(N)\}\le \exp\{-2\lambda^2/3\}+\exp\{-\lambda\},\] for any \lambda>0 and N\ge 1, where \[\tilde{B}_p(N):=\sigma\Gamma_N\left[2\bar{V}(x^*)\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^{T_k}\left(\frac{\gamma_kP_{T_k}}{\Gamma_k(1-P_{T_k})p_iP_{i-1}}\right)^2\right]^{1/2}+\sigma^2\Gamma_N\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{i=1}^{T_k}\frac{\gamma_kP_{T_k}}{\beta_k\Gamma_k(1-P_{T_k})p_i^2P_{i-1}}.\] (c) If X is compact and relation (8.1.35) (instead of (8.1.33)) holds, then both parts (a) and (b) still hold by replacing the first term in the definition of \tilde{B}_d(N) with \gamma_N\beta_N\bar{V}(x^*)/(1-P_{T_N}).
key_lemmas.role: Generic SGS convergence theorem specialized by Corollary 8.3 to concrete parameter choices.

proof.description: Derive the master pathwise inequality from the one-step outer recursion and the SPS inner bound.
Take u=x^* and expectations; the martingale inner products vanish and the second moment is bounded by sigma squared.
For compact X and light-tailed noise, apply the martingale large-deviation bound to the linear noise terms.
Use Markov's inequality and the light-tail condition to control the quadratic noise sum.
For the compact reverse-monotone case, replace the first Bregman telescoping term by the terminal diameter bound.
